6f81:
Study Law at Canterbury Christ Church and join a challenging and vibrant community, led by an experienced team of academics and practitioners, including solicitors, barristers and international lawyers.

This Law degree will enable students to progress to the vocational stage of lawyer’s training, to qualify as either a solicitor or barrister. With a combination of theory and practice, this original and innovative degree in Law will effectively challenge students and give them the opportunity to develop vital and transferable skills needed for a future career in Law and beyond.

Canterbury Christ Church is one of only a few universities across the country which offers a dual qualification to those who choose to take this path: an LLB and Membership of the National Association of Licensed Paralegals. This means that students will graduate with a GradNALP in addition to their LLB, which will enable students to be an official paralegal.

The teaching staff are specialists in a wide range of areas. From human rights and artificial intelligence to corporate and medical, students will learn alongside experts, many of whom are still practising.

Students will also have the option to get involved with practical justice, including opportunities to shadow a local judge and experience live mediations from the in-house Mediation Clinic. This practice will certainly highlight their professional experience and understanding, which will enhance their overall skillset. Through the strong links with the local community, Citizens Advice and the local courts, students will have the opportunity to act as a Community Legal Companion for unrepresented parties at court. This is an excellent opportunity for students to gain hands-on work experience in a legal setting, which will set them up for the world of work post-graduation.
6f8b:
This Law degree will enable students to progress to the vocational stage of lawyer’s training, to qualify as either a solicitor or barrister. This original and innovative course has been designed in consultation with senior managers to give students both a theoretical and practical experience.

The University is one of only a few universities across the country which offers a dual qualification: an LLB and Membership of the National Association of Licensed Paralegals (provided students choose specific module options), which means they graduate with a GradNALP in addition to their LLB enjoying Paralegal status.

As part of this degree, students will have the option to get involved with practical justice including opportunities to shadow a local judge and experience live mediations from the in-house Medication Clinic. Through strong links with the local community, Citizens Advice, and local courts, students will have the opportunity to act as a Community Legal Companion for unrepresented parties at court. This is an excellent opportunity for students to gain hands-on work experience in a legal setting.

In addition to all the LLB degrees being Qualifying Law Degrees, students have designed the degrees in consultation with external stakeholders, such as local law practitioners as well as a range of local organisations. This ensures the University help students to develop the skills which are highly valued by employers, with examples including written and verbal communication, initiative, time management, flexibility and teamwork. Many graduates use these skills to become a barrister or solicitor, but others establish careers in education, public services, HRM, management, as paralegals, chartered secretaries or in financial services. This qualification can also be used to progress on to postgraduate study in law, such as an LLM, or in related areas such as management, marketing and accountancy.
6f83:
Study Law with Criminology and join a challenging, vibrant and friendly community, led by an experienced team of academics, practitioners, solicitors, barristers and international lawyers.

This degree will enable students to progress to the vocational stage of lawyer’s training, to qualify as either a solicitor or barrister. This original and innovative course has been designed in consultation with senior managers to give students both a theoretical and practical experience.

As part of the degree, students will have the option to get involved with practical justice including opportunities to shadow a local judge and experience live mediations from the in-house Medication Clinic. Through the strong links with the local community, Citizens Advice, and local courts, students will have the opportunity to act as a Community Legal Companion for unrepresented parties at court. This is an excellent opportunity for students to gain hands-on work experience in a legal setting.

The course combines the traditional study of law with a progressive approach, meaning students will experience formal directed teaching in the form of lectures, seminars and tutorials, with indirect learning and teaching methods including discussions, student-led seminars, peer-assisted learning, individual and group role play and mooting.
6f89:
The legal profession is well respected and a career in this field is considered by many to be highly prestigious. It therefore requires professionals with excellent academic ability and a strong work ethic. By studying Law with Politics, students can gain a sound understanding of law while studying aspects of politics that will enable them to progress to lawyers training or a career in the field of politics.

Students will be challenged to develop both academically and professionally through a combination of theoretical learning and practical skills development. Students will learn in a supportive, collaborative and friendly community environment.

During the course, students will develop a critical understanding of the main principles, themes and methods of law so that they:

  • Become a conscious legal professional.
  • Acquire and apply their critical mind to the evaluation and appreciation of contemporary socio-legal issues.
  • Experience practical learning as part of the legal education experience.

Throughout the course, students will develop transferable skills that will be essential as they embark on a professional career. Students will build their confidence and abilities in communication, research, evaluation, critical judgement, time management, team working, and meeting tight deadlines. The University will also support students with specialist training in areas such as writing and advocacy skills, and faculty will help to prepare students for the next steps in their career, for example by doing one-to-one mock interview sessions.
6f6r:
The Accounting and Finance course is designed to equip students with the skills and knowledge they will need to pursue a career in the fields of finance or accountancy.

Students will benefit from Christ Church Business School’s extensive links with industry. Guest speakers are regularly invited to share their knowledge with the students and students will have excellent opportunities to undertake work placements, supported by a dedicated placement officer.

The University recognise the importance of professional body accreditation and the course is structured to allow students to gain exemptions from major accounting bodies.

The experienced team has created an engaging course which captures the diversity of the national and global dimensions of finance and accounting, so students will be prepared for all kinds of roles in industry, practice, the service sector or self-employment.

Students can test their skills in a real business environment in the Bloomberg Trading Room, which recreates the high-energy City of London trading environment. This will give students the opportunity to learn the language of finance, discover the inner workings of the markets, and stand out to recruiters with "Bloomberg Certification" Bloomberg Market Concepts (BMC) on their CV. Students will have the opportunity to apply for exemptions from major accounting bodies, such as ACCA, ICAEW, CIMA, & IFA, and students will develop specialist accounting knowledge, critical analysis and interpersonal skills during lectures, seminars, workshops and through a variety of assessments.
6f6s:
BSc Accounting and Finance degree gives students a solid grounding in the challenges of managing organisations, information technology and analytical skills alongside finance and accounting fundamentals.

The foundation year will help students to broaden their industry knowledge and enable them to progress to a related undergraduate degree. It aims to help students develop a strong foundation of business knowledge, alongside academic and transferable skills to ensure they get the most out of their degree-level studies.

Students will benefit from Christ Church Business School’s extensive links with industry. The experienced team has created an engaging course which captures the diversity of the national and global dimensions of finance and accounting, so students will be prepared for all kinds of roles in industry, practice, the service sector or self-employment.

Students will gain experience in applying their knowledge to help solve real-world problems and will develop the skills needed for further academic study and independent learning.

Students can test their skills in a real business environment in the Bloomberg Trading Room, which recreates the high-energy City of London trading environment. This will give students the opportunity learn the language of finance, discover the inner workings of the markets, and stand out to recruiters with "Bloomberg Certification" Bloomberg Market Concepts (BMC) on their CV.
6f70:
Business management is vital in every industry. Those who're keen to develop their critical thinking skills and understand the essential areas of business, then this course covers what they need to know to become a successful business graduate.

Gaining a solid understanding of business management will readily prepare students for a career in a range of sectors and industries, including the finance and technology industries. Not only will students study the fundamental areas of business, finance, HR, marketing and operations, they will also focus on the micro and macro environments in which businesses operate. This will develop their understanding of business structures, whilst expanding their confidence and knowledge with how to handle real-world scenarios.

With such a diverse and professionally-sound curriculum, this course is industry-led, giving students the opportunity to examine and analyse real-life organisational issues within local, regional and national organisations.
6f7z:
Good business management is at the centre of every successful organisation. This Business Management with Foundation Year degree enables students to build their knowledge and understanding of organisations and how they are managed. The foundation year helps students develop the study skills and self-confidence needed for higher education.

Students will study fundamental areas of business, finance, HR, marketing and operations, and the macro and micro environments in which they operate including cultural, social and ethical issues.

Students will have opportunities to examine real-life organisational problems by making the most of the strong links between Christ Church Business School and a wide range of local, regional and national organisations.

The course will introduce students to different organisations and external environments, so they can understand how they operate and are managed as businesses. It is practical in nature, which allows students to begin building their knowledge from day one.

During the foundation year, students will learn about key areas of business and will develop the skills needed to study at degree level. Throughout the degree, students will develop their business and management skills while being exposed to scenarios and real-world problems that will make them think outside the box.
6f8l:
MA Early Childhood Education is aimed at graduates (nationally and internationally) from a variety of backgrounds who wish to expand and deepen their knowledge of young children and their learning from birth to eight years.

Supported by a small team of academics, students will have the opportunity to research and develop specialist areas of expertise within the field. During the programme students will also be encouraged to reflect on the ways this learning supports their professional and career development.

Each year the University is reminded of the transformational potential of education as the students move onto a PhD, are promoted, set up their own business, gain a new role or reignite their passion for an existing one.

The core modules (common across all routes) give students the opportunity to gain insights into the critical educational issues of the day and to develop key postgraduate academic skills. The specialist modules reflect and incorporate the expertise of the teaching team in early childhood research and scholarship. From the first module (Developing Criticality) through to the last (Dissertation) the aim is to support students in developing their knowledge and skills in relation to their professional and/or personal interests.
6f8m:
Being curious and questioning is the starting premise for the MA Education. This course starts with fundamental questions about learning and seeks to examine the complexity of a basic human right; the right to an education. The course challenges students to reflect and review values and philosophies of education and learning drawing upon their own practice. Criticality and self-reflection as key learning attributes.

This course is for those interested and passionate about education and learning and who are committed to adopting a questioning approach. Students may be in a professional role working in school or educational setting or whose work involves a substantial component of the design and delivery of training within their organisation. Students may be at the beginning of their career, looking forward, or in a more established leadership role. A student may be a volunteer working in an education setting, or in a support role.

The core modules (common across all routes) give students the opportunity to gain insights into the critical educational issues of the day and to develop key postgraduate academic skills. The specialist modules reflect and incorporate the expertise of the teaching team in education research and scholarship. From the first module (Developing Criticality) through to the last (Dissertation) the aim is to support students in developing their knowledge and skills in relation to their professional and/or personal interests.

This course will engage students with theories about learning for adults and children and will provide students with opportunities to critically reflect on their role as an educator, as a leader, as a stakeholder in the provision of learning. Critical thinking, research and evidence informed practice, reflection and review are embedded in all the areas of study.
6f95:
The MA Filmmaking offers a unique blend of practical production skills, professional knowledge and academic study as well as opportunities for students to become a researcher in their own right.

The University have designed the course to be taught through a combination of intensive workshop sessions, online interactive and self-directed teaching, as well as group and individual tutorials. The programme provides intensive instruction in cinematography, camerawork, sound recording and design, non-linear editing, scriptwriting, producing and directing.

The course is taught by a team of experienced educators who have had professional careers in a related sector and/or are internationally recognised researchers in their field. A group of non-academic partners and advisors also contribute to the delivery of the programme, in the forms of visiting talks, debates and discussions, contributing to assignment briefs, and offering networking opportunities. These professionals have significant experience as media creators.

This course is unique that it is delivered alongside multiple degree routes in the broader Creative and Cultural Industries subject areas, which enables students to have a multi and interdisciplinary learning experience and meet and collaborate with a range of creative professionals.
6f8p:
This course in Media and Communications offers a stimulating programme with a unique blend of academic study, professional knowledge and skills development as well as opportunities for students to become a researcher in their own right.

The University know that people's lives are busy, so they've designed the course to be taught through a combination of intensive in person sessions, online interactive and self-directed teaching, as well as group and individual tutorials. This programme will equip students with highly employable skills and advanced knowledge base to critically understand and navigate this environment both as an individual and in their professional roles.

The course is for everyone who wishes to study the fascinating fields of Media and Communications at postgraduate level. It is designed for graduates who have completed a degree in a related field and wish to develop their career prospects; or graduates who have completed a degree in a different discipline but now wish to pursue a career in Media and Communications

It is also designed for those who already work in a related role and who wish to enhance their effectiveness and confidence in the workplace or to develop their career prospects.
898e:
Individuals can advance their careers and make a meaningful impact on society with the MA Social Work program. This two-year, full-time course equips students with the knowledge, skills, and professional experience needed to support and protect vulnerable individuals at all stages of life. Fully accredited by Social Work England (SWE), the course integrates academic study, hands-on skills training, and extensive practice placements to ensure that students develop the expertise required for effective and ethical social work practice.

Through engaging lectures, seminars, and practical training, students will learn from academic tutors, experienced practitioners, and individuals with lived experience of social services. The state-of-the-art facilities, including the Hydra simulated skills suite and courtroom, provide invaluable opportunities for students to refine their abilities in case analysis, report writing, and court proceedings.

In addition to 30 skills development days, students will undertake two significant practice placements—70 days in the first year and 100 days in the second—working in diverse settings to gain hands-on experience with children, families, vulnerable adults, and individuals with mental health needs.

At the heart of this course is a commitment to social justice and inclusion. Students will explore the impact of structural inequalities, social policies, and intersecting factors that affect individuals’ well-being. Through research and reflective practice, they will challenge preconceptions in a supportive environment, developing the listening and advocacy skills essential for empowering those in need.

Upon successful completion, students will be eligible to apply for registration with Social Work England (SWE), opening the door to a fulfilling and impactful career. They are encouraged to join the program and take the next step in shaping a fairer, more inclusive society.
6f8t:
The Canterbury Christ Church MBA International is primarily designed for recent university graduates who have little or no prior work experience but are interested in developing a future career in international business and management. The course aims to engage and educate students in preparation for managerial and career roles in the international business arena. The course has a strong emphasis on employability for careers in business, management and policy making.

The MBA International will encourage stringent and critical professional development, engaging students with the systematic review of international business theories, policies and practice. It will reflect an international body of thinking and study, and investigation of international business problems in the current, complex environment.

It will help students gain insights into the latest trends in international business, as well as UK private and public sector organisations. With the experience of the leading team of researchers and professional practice tutors, the University will ensure the MBA International course maintains a pragmatic focus to enhance students' business career.

The course will provide students with the necessary knowledge, skills and expertise required in a dynamic, unpredictable and unprecedented global trading environment. Graduates can also engage in further research on the MPhil/PhD programme.
